body.x: In the Star Wars series, there are certain scenes where the Jedi are able to move objects with the power of the Force. Sound like more movie nonsense? Believe it or not, but it is now possible to do something quite like this in real life.

Using the headset called the Star Wars Force Trainer, which was released by NeuroSky in 2009, you can move a ball inside a tube by mental concentration alone. The dry sensors that are in contact with your forehead detect brain waves and communicate this information through the headset via Bluetooth to the main force trainer device. As concentration (beta waves) increases, the ball rises, and as you become more relaxed (alpha waves), the ball descends once again. This device became famous under the nickname of “superpower headset,” and in Korea it became well-known after appearing on various TV shows.

After this, NeuroSky got busy exploring all of the different possible ways that this technology could be applied to real life. One of the things that resulted from their efforts is the Mindset. The Mindset is an apparatus that allows you to monitor your brain waves on a screen and make gains in your ability to concentrate through training your brain. In other words, you can see how your brain waves are altered by the music you listen to and focus your concentration on moving objects inside of a game. The designers claim that if you train like this for thirty minutes every day, you can learn to concentrate better and study more efficiently. The Mindset can also function as a multimedia headset with a variety of functions including playing games, listening to music, and talking on the phone without using your hands.
At the NeuroSky booth at KES 2012, you can check out both the Star Wars Force Trainer and the Mindset. Now is your chance to test your ability as a Jedi. May the Force be with you!
